children: lost more than 20% in the premarket on Tuesday even after announcing positive outcomes in two late-stage trials testing barzolvolimab, its experimental therapy for a skin condition known as urticaria (hives).
Shares of the New Jersey-based Celldex
soared initially after the company said its Phase 3 EMBARQ-CSU1 and EMBARQ-CSU2 trials for its lead candidate met the primary endpoint and key secondary endpoints.

However, the stock plunged as investors parsed through the results, which were based on Sept. 9 data cut from the studies involving adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria who had undergone prior H1-antihistamine therapy.

According to the company, the studies met the primary endpoint of mean change in weekly urticaria activity score from baseline to Week 12 and all key secondary endpoints, indicating clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvements in disease activity.
